## Business

**427-26** 

Order: That the sum of One Hundred Fifty-Seven Thousand Dollars ($157,000) be and the same is hereby transferred from Salary Reserve (0010-996-5110) to the following accounts:

Sponsors: Carey McDonald

Attachments: Final Paper 427-26 Assistant Department Head Salaries Transfer

Councillor McDonald said Paper #427-26 is the appropriation that accompanies the updates in the Assistant Director Salaries and asked Chuck if that is correct.

Chuck gave the committee a brief overview of the Paper. The proposed transfer moves $157,000 from salary reserve into department salary accounts: $15,000 for Psrking salaries, $46,000 for Controller salaries, $16,000 for Assessor salaries, $16,000 for Treasurer salaries, $13,000 for OSPCD salaries, $16,000 for Engineering salaries, $13,000 for City Clerk salaries, $6,000 for Information Technology salaries, and $16,000 for DPW Administration salaries. He explained we recently updated the ordinances for the Assistant Department Head Contract. The City and Teamsters executed a two-year agreement covering July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2026. The appropriation provides a 3% cost-of-living increase for FY2025 and another 3% for FY2026, while FY2027 is excluded because the City is negotiating that year and no union salary increases have been established. Eligible employees receive the longevity or education benefit that applied to the department’s bargaining unit: an additional 3% of base pay for at least 10 years of service or a bachelor’s degree, and an additional 4% for at least 25 years of service or a master’s degree. The 4% benefit is additive to the 3% benefit, not a replacement for it. The calculation includes current employees and former employees who were covered during the agreement period, including two separate Assistant Department Heads in the IT area. The transfer is intended to pay all retroactive amounts due through June 30, 2026. The team chose a full, transparent transfer for every listed department rather than relying on existing account balances. For OSPCD, one position is grant-funded and one is not; the general-fund salary account associated with the non-grant-funded position would otherwise produce surplus free cash when the fiscal year closes.

Councillor McDonald clarified this goes back and checks former employees who may have been covered by this agreement.

Chuck said that is correct, the IT Dept and DPW. The DPW had two Assistant Dept Heads as well as the IT Assistant Director and this ensures they will receive any benefits during that time.

Councillor Luong asked about DPW certifications?

Chuck explained that the Assistant Department Head education benefit applies strictly to a bachelor’s degree or, at the higher threshold, a master’s degree. DPW’s separate contract contains stipends for specific certifications, but those stipends are outside this education benefit.

Councillor Condon asked if this is 3% per year for 2025 & 2026?

Chuck said it's two years of retroactive compensation. The appropriation also includes any eligible longevity or education benefits accrued during those fiscal years.

Councillor McDonald asked Chuck to clarify if the initial intention was to use existing appropriations where possible, but staff determined that a single full transfer was cleaner and more transparent.

Chuck said the latter. The initial intent was to use the existing appropriations to cover all of them but to make it clear for example OSPCD because the majority of their positions are grant funded there would definately be flexibility in their salary account to cover the transfer of $13,000. Grant funded salaries woud be a surplus at the end of the year and fall under free cash. These transfers are the full amount and we wanted to be fully transparent so no Dept was left off the list.

A motion was made by Councillor Luong, seconded by Councillor Condon, that the Order be recommended favorably to the City Council. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

Yea: 5 - Councillor McDonald, Councillor Taylor, Councillor Condon, Councillor Luong and Councillor Sica

**428-26** 

Order: That the sum of Two Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars ($220,000) be and

the same is hereby transferred from Salary Reserve (0010-996-5110) to Police Salaries (0010-210-5120).

Sponsors: Carey McDonald

Attachments: Final Paper 428-26 Police Patrolman's Salary Transfer

The Clerk read Paper #428-26 into the record: Order that the sum of $200,000 be and the same is hereby transferred from Salary Reserve to Police Salaries.

Chuck explained this is the Police Patrolman's salary. We had a memorandum of agreement with the Patrol Association expired June 30, 2025. After broader negotiations were paused, the Association and City reached a one-year FY2026 agreement on September 30, 2026, covering employees through June 30, 2026. The agreement provides a 3% FY2026 cost-of-living increase and includes language and shift changes. The retirement-related payment increases from $10 to $50 per day, matching the standard used by the City’s other bargaining units. The 3% increase applies not only to base pay but also to police wage supplements. For approximately 75 patrol officers, the relevant compensation components include $5.4 million in base pay, $171,000 in hazardous-duty pay, $323,000 in shift differentials, $655,000 in educational incentive payments, $66,000 in senior longevity, $247,000 in sick-time buyback, $307,000 in holiday pay, and $74,000 in non-education longevity. The covered compensation totals approximately $7.2 million; applying the 3% increase produces approximately $217,000 to $237,000 in additional costs, supporting the requested $220,000 transfer from salary reserve to police salaries.

Councillor McDonald asked how many employees are in the Police Patrolman Unit.

Chuck said there were originally 78 members and there are 75 currently on the payroll.

A motion was made by Councillor Sica, seconded by Councillor Luong, that the Order be recommended favorably to the City Council. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 5 - Councillor McDonald, Councillor Taylor, Councillor Condon, Councillor Luong and Councillor Sica
